steps.say: The commonest blockage on the right side of a child's heart is at the pulmonary valve itself. Valvular pulmonary stenosis causes 8 to 10 percent of all congenital cardiac defects. Most children with isolated pulmonary valve stenosis feel entirely well, and the lesion is picked up from a murmur before it ever causes symptoms.
steps.tx: **Valvular pulmonary stenosis** is the most common form of **right ventricular outflow obstruction**, accounting for **8-10%** of all congenital cardiac defects. The valve domes in systole with commissural fusion, the right ventricle hypertrophies behind the obstruction, and most mild cases need only surveillance since the gradient often stays stable for years.

steps.say: A thick unyielding pulmonary valve in a short child with neck webbing should trigger one diagnosis. Dysplastic pulmonary stenosis from PTPN11 gene mutation is the hallmark heart lesion of Noonan syndrome, seen in 50 to 60 percent of patients. Unlike the thin doming valve, this dysplastic valve responds poorly to balloon dilation and usually needs surgery.
steps.tx: **Noonan syndrome** carries dysplastic **pulmonary valve stenosis** with **PTPN11 gene mutation** as its hallmark cardiovascular anomaly in **50-60%** of patients. The leaflets are severely thickened with little commissural fusion, so balloon valvuloplasty often fails and surgical valvotomy is required, alongside screening for hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and bleeding diathesis.

Balloon valvuloplasty is the treatment of choice
Excellent relief of gradient in most children

steps.say: Opening a stenotic pulmonary valve no longer needs open heart surgery in most children. Percutaneous balloon pulmonary valvuloplasty is the definitive treatment for moderate to severe stenosis once the peak Doppler gradient crosses 40 to 50 millimetres of mercury. A catheter balloon simply splits the fused commissures and the gradient falls immediately.
steps.tx: **Pulmonary balloon valvuloplasty**, delivered percutaneously, is the treatment of choice for moderate to severe pulmonary stenosis when the peak Doppler gradient exceeds **40-50 mmHg**. The balloon tears fused commissures without cardiopulmonary bypass, critical neonatal stenosis needs prostaglandin cover until the procedure, and restenosis is uncommon except in dysplastic Noonan valves.

nodes.label: Echocardiography measures peak Doppler gradient across the pulmonary valve
Gradient above 40-50 mmHg marks moderate to severe stenosis needing relief
Catheter balloon splits the fused commissures under imaging guidance
Gradient falls at once and restenosis stays uncommon outside Noonan valves

steps.tx: Watch the sequence at the pulmonary valve during this procedure. A catheter crosses the narrowed orifice, the balloon inflates inside the domed valve, and its waist suddenly gives way as the fused commissures split apart. That controlled tear is **balloon pulmonary valvuloplasty**, relieving obstruction at once without opening the chest or placing the child on bypass.
steps.say: During balloon pulmonary valvuloplasty the catheter balloon inflates inside the domed valve and splits its fused commissures. The obstruction is relieved at once without open surgery or bypass.

steps.say: The commonest congenital aortic valve lesion is often silent for decades. A bicuspid aortic valve is the most frequent congenital anomaly of the aortic valve, affecting boys three to four times more often than girls. It stenoses, leaks, dilates the aorta, and dissects, so every diagnosed child needs lifelong aortic surveillance.
steps.tx: **Congenital aortic stenosis** most often means a **bicuspid aortic valve**, the most frequent congenital valve anomaly, with a male to female ratio of **3:1 to 4:1** and a population prevalence of 1 to 2 percent. The two leaflets calcify early to produce stenosis, the valve often leaks, and the ascending aorta dilates over time, so echocardiographic surveillance of valve and aorta continues for life.

steps.say: Measured gradients are deciding the fate of a stenotic aortic valve. Disease is mild when the mean gradient sits under 25 millimetres of mercury, moderate between 25 and 40, and severe when the peak gradient exceeds 50 to 64 or the mean crosses 40. Severe gradients with symptoms are referred promptly for balloon dilation or surgery.
steps.tx: **Aortic stenosis gradients** by echocardiography grade severity: mild when mean gradient is under **25 mmHg**, moderate between **25-40 mmHg**, and severe when peak gradient exceeds **50-64 mmHg** or mean gradient exceeds **40 mmHg**. Doppler severity grading, as shown in stenotic valves, guides whether the child is watched, balloon dilated, or sent for surgical relief.

steps.say: One click separates aortic from pulmonary stenosis at the bedside. Aortic stenosis throws an early systolic ejection click at the apex that ignores breathing, while the pulmonary click softens when the child breathes in. As either valve stiffens with severe disease, its click fades and may vanish altogether.
steps.tx: A **systolic ejection click** localises the stenotic valve: the aortic click is heard at the **apex** and does not vary with respiration, unlike the **pulmonary ejection click** at the left upper border which **softens on inspiration**. With advancing severity and immobile leaflets both clicks fade, so a vanishing click in a known stenotic valve warns of worsening obstruction.

steps.say: Growing children outgrow artificial valves, but one operation grows with them. The Ross operation moves the child's own pulmonary valve into the aortic position and places a homograft where the pulmonary valve was. The living autograft lasts for decades without blood thinners, though both valves need lifelong follow up.
steps.tx: The **Ross procedure**, or Ross operation, replaces the diseased aortic valve with the patient's own **pulmonary autograft**, with a **homograft** placed in the pulmonary position. It is the preferred aortic valve substitute for growing children because the autograft grows, resists infection, and needs no anticoagulation, trading one valve disease for monitored disease in two well tolerated positions.

steps.say: A friendly overtalkative child with puffy eyes and a harsh murmur is signalling one microdeletion. Supravalvular aortic stenosis from elastin gene deletion on chromosome 7q11 is the signature lesion of Williams syndrome. The narrowed ascending aorta needs surgical patching, and the coronary arteries demand respect during induction of anaesthesia.
steps.tx: **Williams syndrome** features **supravalvular aortic stenosis** from elastin gene (**ELN**) deletion on **chromosome 7q11.23**, a hemizygous microdeletion of about 25 genes. The hourglass narrowing sits above the valve with elfin facies, cocktail party speech, and infantile hypercalcaemia, and anaesthesia is hazardous because adherent aortic wall can obstruct the coronary ostia.
